gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-devanagari: Noto Serif Devanagari reads like a well-thumbed novel, a classic serif with curves that thin just slightly at the tops. Flavors is the playful shouter beside it, towering and bluntly drawn, and the two feel like a joker and a librarian sharing a shelf.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-dives-akuru: Flavors is all towering, pencil-stub lowercase and diagonals as hefty as its stems. Noto Serif Dives Akuru follows with short capitals among tall small letters and a soft contrast you feel more than see, so paragraphs would drift along gently.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Flavors has stems and arches of identical thickness, with no thick-thin shift anywhere, which gives it a blunt, crayon-simple swagger. And Noto Serif Dogra settles in beneath with capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so a longer passage would read with a faint, bookish rhythm.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-ethiopic: Whimsical is the first word for Flavors, every glyph drawn as if with a single tip. Noto Serif Ethiopic brings the opposite strength: words that sit as solid blocks, with the slight reed-pen thickening of a text serif.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-georgian: Noto Serif Georgian reads with authority, its lowercase swollen like tightly coiled rope and its stroke modulation subtle but visible. gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-gujarati: Noto Serif Gujarati has a bookish, authoritative manner, with oversized counters and joins that ease only slightly in weight. Flavors is best at shouting, every letter part carrying equal mass, while Noto Serif Gujarati is best at the friendly, mild-contrast work of carrying text.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi: Flavors comes in whimsical and commanding, with horizontals exactly as heavy as its verticals. Noto Serif Gurmukhi follows with a generous x-height and a gradual weight change, so a body size a step or two down from the heading feels natural.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-hebrew: Tall, sturdy and a bit cheeky. Flavors holds one constant pen width throughout, while Noto Serif Hebrew, a text serif, shifts its strokes just enough to be noticed, so the heading plays loud and the text answers with quiet authority.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Noto Serif Kannada pairs big counters with a tall lowercase, giving a traditional, literary feel. And Flavors, drawn as if with a ballpoint pen, brings the whimsy, a quality the text serif's slimmer horizontals gently temper.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Noto Serif Khmer reads like a classic serif cut in letterpress, with tall lowercase sitting close to its capitals and only mild thinning at the curves. And Flavors, with round letters as heavy as its straight ones, would make any longer passage feel like a loud title sitting over a steady, authoritative text.
